prompt: Create a three-row, one-column transparent atlas. The reference is a labeled contact sheet with three rows: row 1 exact target bubble-necropolis-tomb-stone-stairs-up; row 2 exact target bubble-desert-sandstone-and-sand-stairs-up; row 3 exact target bubble-desert-sandstone-and-sand-stairs-down. Each row's first labeled image is its canonical source; the remaining six are that same object's current views. Output one BOTTOM orthographic underside per matching row, in the same order. For each object, source and side views show a solid opaque stone wedge supporting the stairs. Looking upward, no upper treads or step faces can show through. Draw the complete matching footprint as a continuous opaque stone underside/base slab with source-specific stone material, retaining each object's native footprint and palette (Necropolis gold carved stone; Desert sandy sandstone). Do not invent a generic wood tray, do not reuse another row's material, no upside-down treads, no hazards, no frontal staircase face, no open gaps. Each result must be a flat bottom-plane view with the same plan extents as its own TOP, centered, complete, isolated in transparent cell with broad gutters; no text, labels, or grid. Crisp source-matched pixel-art. Inferred underside art, not recovered pixels or calibrated 3D.

reference_inputs.role: each row binds canonical source and current six-view identity
